name: Захист від шаху
description:
When a piece is attacked you can often choose how to defend it. The same goes for an attack on the king (check).

You already know how you can get your king out of check. By moving, capturing or blocking. In a game it is up to you to decide what is best.

In example 1, all three methods are good. But that’s not always the case. Just look at example 2. Here, one way to get out of check is clearly the best.
Sometimes, you have no choice. See example 3.

In this lesson, you have to pick the best way to get out of check.
Do you use moving, capturing or blocking?

You have done this before, in one of the Pawn level lessons. But now there are more chessmen on the board.

What do you have to do?
Your king is in check. Play the best move to get out of check.

examples.text:
White has three ways to get out of check.
He can move his king, his knight can take the bishop, or he can move the bishop to block the attack.
All three are good moves. White can choose the one he fancies most.

You could move your king. That’s probably what most players would do (without thinking).
Or you could use the bishop for blocking.
Both moves help to get your king out of check. But there is a better move! Do you see it?
White can take the rook!
This gets the king out of check and wins White 5 points

Black’s rook is checking the king.
The red square is the only place where the king is safe from the rook. However, the king cannot go there. From a distance, Black’s bishop looks at the red square.
White could also take the rook with his queen. But that would not be smart. The bishop protects the rook.
Taking the rook would win White 5 points. Losing his queen would lose him 9. 9 minus 5 is a total loss of 4 points.

Fortunately, there is another way to get out of check.
The white bishop can go between the rook and the king.
King saved and no points lost.

texts: Neutralize the threat without losing material.
